subject: Television & Streaming
title: Propaganda on the Small Screen
description: One-minute skill: Propaganda on the Small Screen.

hook.text: In the Soviet Union, television was a state-controlled tool. Every broadcast served the party's message.

buildup.text: State television presented a curated version of reality—happy workers, bountiful harvests, and a benevolent government.

discovery.text: When satellite television arrived, citizens could see Western broadcasts.

twist.text: Mikhail Gorbachev's glasnost allowed freer media.

climax.text: Television in authoritarian states is a paradox: the best tool for control until it becomes the best tool for revolt.

punchline.text: The same screen that spreads lies can expose them.

quiz.question: What happened to Soviet state television's credibility when citizens accessed satellite broadcasts?
options: Trust collapsed as people saw the contrast between propaganda and reality
